text:
Predicates:
InCity(x, y) ::: x is in city y.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
City(y) ::: y is a city.
State(y) ::: y is a state.
InSameState(x, y) ::: x and y are in the same state.
DifferentStates(x, y) ::: x and y are in different states.
OnlyOneState(x, y) ::: city x can only be in one state y.
Question: 
StPierre(y) ∧ Bismarck(z) → InSameState(y, z) ::: If y is St Pierre and z is Bismarck, then they are in the same state.
Premises:
Montana(montana) ∧ City(butte) ∧ City(helena) ∧ City(missoula) ::: Montana is a state, and Butte, Helena, Missoula are cities.
InCity(whiteSulphurSprings, montana) ∧ InCity(butte, montana) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in Montana.
City(stPierre) ∧ ¬InState(stPierre, montana) ::: St Pierre is a city not in Montana.
InCity(butte, stPierre) → ¬InCity(butte, stPierre) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x ∀y (InCity(x, y) → ∀z (InCity(x, z) → z = y)) ::: A city can only be in one state.
Conclusion:
InSameState(stPierre, bismarck) ::: St Pierre and Bismarck are in the same state.
